text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

Four women on a panel isn't evidence of anything. Planning departments and municipal HR skew heavily female, so all-women panels arise by chance often enough that the composition carries almost no information. Raising it would signal that you read a loss as bias, which is the fastest way to lose future goodwill in a small professional world.

Also, your credential advantage matters less than you think. Director roles are political: council relations, contentious hearings, angry residents. "Extensive public consultation experience" is a direct read on that, while a master's and a licence read on technical work you'd now be supervising.

Do pursue the feedback — two weeks of silence is worth one polite follow-up to the hiring contact, framed as development, not grievance.
